## Design

### 2026-10-06 – October 6

**9.5h**

October 6

Though this was my first time designing a PCB, I still ended up creating a very basic Schematic. I originally began by following a GitHub tutorial, but that got quickly got too confusing, so I restarted  and began with finding KiCad Footprint Libraries and figuring out the electronics theory.

![01-matrix-research](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/2844f40d75c5796160a3fc0e4111c849d99f9a8e8a85075c33664b29f76958e6.jpg)
This was the Matrix Research I had to complete

To find the Libraries, I had to hunt down custom ones for Cherry MX switches, looking up the dimensions of a 1U keycap spacing, and looking into the pinout of an Arduino Pro Micro, but I later changed this to a Raspberry Pi

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/1ce5be343caff0c61ab4016f752b8d9515fbfa89795fed86c663ede11e9eeec6.png)

To understand the electronics theory, I had to research Keyboard matric functions, I also learned that I needed a 1N4148 diode next to every single switch to prevent something called ghosting. I also needed to know which way the electrical current flows in the PCB. I also learned how to use Global Labels to keep nets clean.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/6d660de9637e0b907a25daf5680e9168ea810fe933ba5206ebef935523ce8c37.png)
I also completed the 61 key ANSI layout as part of the placement plan along with matrix coordinate on each key

Later I found out that I didn't need a custom library, so I used the kicad ones, so I installed the kicad footprint verification
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/96064cbf2dae7636ce794e34669d33f09c4712a7b40dfe2b68e3ad4e3d0c8126.png)

It took me a while to get to this stage at the pace I was working, and this was my first switch and anti-ghosting diode, and I followed the same method for each key
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/4aad322bfb6f143ab1dbf59bddeb86e5bbb4e1c6f556318b76ef5f5194c42ceb.png)

My next step was the number keys of 14 switch diode pairs, following the same COL to switch to diode anode; diode cathode to ROW
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/4d90e7126712b07fb729884dd06a1cf8b81b48d4b9f6ad75a873305a741dd5c3.png)

I later individually created each of the following keys and typed up the following information to specify which was which
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/2968c0a8a03da4ef494fb9d00208e11051d0f48078f3af143ee9bd9a53434c6b.png)

My next step was  working with the Raspberry Pi Pico Controller and GPIO net labels, where I attached all labels and rows
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/5f12dc12cfa9dc35a2a9fd2210207e06fdea44fa817c951d62eeb21929e9158b.png)

By this point after many errors I made accidentally and going back and forth, I completed the full schematic
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/c91cceff1e5670762f1b32b61f960f69a1cca61d0eba6e4534c9dbc367dc4ae5.png)

I later realized I missed something, I had to set up the Reset circuit and firmware flashing mode to use the onboard BOOTSEL button
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/d6bd2181e24846ba51d9f8a30a60647065539afe7f0dd30ba3d5dba011afa4a8.png)

### 2026-10-07 – October 7

**10h**

October 7

Now I began the actual PCB Portion. For PCB Layout, routing, and vias. I placed grid components, set up custom user grids and manual trace routing. I had to figure out how to route lines on both the front and back copper layers and sue plated holes (vias) to leapfrog the intersecting wires without short circuiting the board. I next had to do DRC Troubleshooting and Manufacturing setup, I threw quite a bit of errors, so I had to define an Edge.Cuts layer to outline the physical board, and I manually set up a copper filled zone to isolate electrical traces

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/885b0c0cc5bddd3665594564afee76354b5f7117bd011f15a4461a1ef92a90b1.png)
I created my board outline, and the space above is reserved for the controller, the boundary was 295x168mm

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/eab954a873282cca162a78d8e920870463b7103c9327fb3bdca17ff2b42283ef.png)
I created my first switch row of 14 footprints using 19.05mm key spacing

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/942b03c3524fabad6b11df0404272491656dd57b52222f556d02fd2b44e51a5a.png)
Next I completed the remaining 61 switches in ANSI layout including the spacebar where the key is the center.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/c3bc702737a021fe5a6d49c9a58fac6d1a9b3909316d45e9701b576ea9dede89.png)
One 1N4148 diode was placed on each switch, on the back of the board between key rows, this is to prevent ghost key presses, an issue that arised for many other people that completed this project

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/bd0b317dc335715baf4aee61fdf86eacbc8f3ac63f42f7975988054d51fce02e.png)
I added the Pico footprint, reset button, and 4 3.2mm mounting holes. I still need to plan to create a casing for the keyboard based on this

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/625b72ee99f4c3e56e71418c850e5b3e35eb97e628f5baa8a03fde9f128c8062.png)
Copper tracks were added between each switch and the diode, these are the individual key connections before the shared matrix wiring is completed

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/0b6b56f8961bd738425d091deb2750fc97ec065e7eeccbe2dce3432145c802c7.png)
With this step I achieved complete signal routing as row and column connections were routed to Pico across front and back copper layers. The vias connect tracks between layers where they were needed

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/5a519c2b78881e31534b583dcee24f203fd03819496d71a958b3f3ca4a4b945b.png)
Filled ground planes on both sides of the PCB. KiCad did leave some clearance around unrelated tracks and pads. Apparently the thermal connections link ground pads to the pours while making the pads easier to solder

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/57cc32490635e3243c4068b93a2888d7e6416f411c1d1504c7e2824c417accc0.png)
I created a Key legend, board identification, assembly instructions to the silkscreen layers. After this there were some errors, which I ended up fixing

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/3jjjr94n6OVBuAuok83iCpwSTn9oI9Z0/1ccebb1bf9a8c59374a5aab74a32cd02d4ad2d0dcf79b6c4073d05719be1d418.png)
KiCad displayed the PCB in it's 3D viewer. For some reason the CherryMX model's didn't work so I would need to troubleshoot why the keycaps and switches are absent

Honest Note: I did use ChatGPT to help me understand the process when designing this PCB, along with helping me fix whatever errors I had. It also helped me take screenshots as my windows computer wouldn't let me on my wireless keyboard, therefore the blue cursor in several screenshots.

The next hour-ish (1-1.5) I've dedicated to creating firmware, I used Python ( a language I am quite good at ) using KMK, which runs on the CircuitPython on the Raspberry Pi Pico. I configured Matrix Wiring, Diode Direction, Key Layout, Fn Layer, USB Keyboard mode. I then ran desktop simulations for typing, wrote and tested the firmware files.

After this I spent the next 0.5 hour updating everything to github, and pushing changes to get stuff done.
